advances: A finite orbit and volume inequality allowing missing parity classes and arbitrary maximal root geometry.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
The midpoint has integer base by parity, and convexity gives the first inclusion. It contains a half-scale copy of a positive fiber, so $F(z)\in P$. Brunn–Minkowski gives the volume-root inequality. If $w_z<m_{[z]}$, then $w_{F(z)}>w_z$. If $w_z=m_{[z]}$ and $z\ne v_{[z]}$, then $|v_{[z]}|^2\le |z|^2$ and
$$
|F(z)|^2=\tfrac12(|z|^2+|v_{[z]}|^2)-\tfrac14|z-v_{[z]}|^2<|z|^2.
$$
The pair $(-w_z,|z|^2)$ strictly decreases lexicographically at every nonfixed point. Finiteness gives termination, and $F(z)=z$ is equivalent to $z=v_{[z]}$. In each class a preimage of $y$ must be $2y-v_c$, giving the multiplicity bound and in particular at most $2^n$ preimages. Repeatedly substituting the Minkowski inclusion gives the displayed dyadic inclusion.

For the absolute bound write $x=w_z^{1/d}$ and $t=m_{[z]}^{1/d}-x\ge0$. The binomial formula gives $(2x+t)^d-(2x)^d\ge(x+t)^d-x^d$ since each term in the difference is a nonnegative constant times a power of the initial argument. Combine with $w_{F(z)}\ge (2x+t)^d/2^d$. For sharpness take one integer coordinate on $[0,2]$ and fibers $(s+(1-s)z/2)K$ with a fixed unit-volume $d$-body $K$ and $0<s<1$. The real family is convex because the positive scale is affine, and it is a compact full-dimensional body with exactly three positive integer fibers. The even maximizer is $2$ and the edge $0\to1$ gives growth divided by the initial deficit equal to $(((1+s)/2)^d-s^d)/(1-s^d)$, which tends to $2^{-d}$ as $s\downarrow0$. For any fixed larger integer dimension take the product with $[0,1/2]^{n-1}$ in the additional base coordinates, which adds no sampled sites.

statement:
Let $d\ge1$ and let $P$ be the nonempty finite positive-fiber base set of a convex body in $\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$. Write $K_z$ for its actual fibers and $w_z=|K_z|$. In each occupied coordinatewise parity $c$ choose a maximizer $v_c$ of $w_z$ minimizing $|v_c|^2$ among its maximizers, with remaining ties arbitrary, and put $m_c=w_{v_c}$. The map $F(z)=(z+v_{[z]})/2$ sends $P$ into itself, has at most one preimage per occupied class for every target, and every orbit terminates at a chosen $v_c$. Its edges satisfy
$$
(K_z+K_{v_{[z]}})/2\subseteq K_{F(z)},\quad
w_{F(z)}^{1/d}\ge(w_z^{1/d}+m_{[z]}^{1/d})/2,\quad
w_{F(z)}-w_z\ge 2^{-d}(m_{[z]}-w_z).
$$
Along $z_0=z,\ldots,z_k=F^k(z)$ one has $2^{-k}K_z+\sum_{j<k}2^{j-k}K_{v_{[z_j]}}\subseteq K_{z_k}$. The absolute-growth coefficient $2^{-d}$ is sharp.
title: Terminating midpoint forest for parity volume maximizers
